I've been wanting to grow my own food for a while now. I have a flat area that is about 12 foot by 7 foot that currently just has stones on it. It gets sun most of the day (I'm in Scotland so sun can be quite rare). Would I need to build a box like thing to fill with compost? I'm not sure how to get started basically.

Can anyone advise what would be good to grow in a limited area like that. Only thing I can think of is potatos, carrots, general common vegetables. Is there anything else that's good to grow in this part of the planet?

I have another area but it is occupied by chickens. If anyone can suggest bushes/greenery that chickens won't destroy that would be great too.
I'm not sure on what chickens won't eat. What do you want to grow? What do you want to eat? Have you read the beginner's guide?

The chickens are kept in a secure run (fox proof) so they can't get to the food I'd be growing. They could do with more bushes to hide in/attract insects but everything I plant for them gets annihilated by the chickens.

I didn't notice the beginners guide before posting sorry. I'll have a peek now.

Well like I said I don't know anything about raising chickens. Imagine if you put something thorny in there like a rose bush or perhaps raspberries they probably wouldn't hurt it. Short of this I would go ahead and plant whatever you like and then put a cage around it so that the chickens can't attack it then after about a year so when it's nice and sturdy you can go ahead and remove the cage.

Definitely grow what is native to your climate. Potatoes are always a safe bet and honestly who doesn't love potatoes. Carrots I wouldn't attempt honestly. If you want nice carrots you need to have a thick marshy soil with no rocks and no nematodes. You don't know what you have under those stones.

I know nothing about chickens but you should probably keep them away at least while the plants are small. Just trampling a seedling is enough to kill it.

If you want to grow green stuff to eat I would go for kale, its hardy as fuck. Lettuce and spinach are honestly so much worse. But I've never been to your part of the world might be shit for kale.

Basically a safe bet is to take off those rocks and either fence your chickens in or fence your garden in. Once that is done see how compacted the soil is. If its been used as a patio or something you might want to loosen the soil and get rid of big stones. Potatoes don't care too much about this kind of thing so that's why I suggested it. When you do this digging take a shovel and take out big chunks and flip them sort of and break it up a bit. You are mostly trying to get rid of stones which you might find annoying later. Its spring time soon so go find some potatoes. You need seeding potatoes, so you can't just buy some at the store. They won't sprout because they are gassed. At that point just let them sprout in a paper bag until you are sure its planting season. Then pull them out and plant them sprout side up. You can cut them, but that's honestly like a "saving mah potatoes" mentality. By planting the whole potato you are giving them the best shot. Just leave them in and let them grow, watering and stuff as you need to. If you don't like weeding, mulch or tarp them. Its certainly cost effective for a small garden.

This. Just a bit to add. First clear out the stones and replace with mulch. Leaves, grass clippings or even wood chips. This start rebuilding the soil. If you go out into the forest and look on the ground its mostly leaves and wood. Dig into those leaves, look closely and you will find all kinds of life. This is what you need to start creating the organic matter that makes plants thrive. This is why mulch is the first step in a successful and long lasting garden.
